message:
fix(ui,host): an id beat a class, and one target never got /utf-8

The update banner was on screen before sign-in and stayed there. `.hidden` is a class
and `#updateBar { display: flex }` is an id, so the id won and adding the class did
nothing. The script had been doing exactly what it was written to do the whole time.
One rule fixes it.

Why the test agreed is the more useful part. It asked classList.contains('hidden'),
which was true for the entire life of the bug -- reading the intention instead of the
result. It now reads getComputedStyle().display with a rect and a hit test, and a new
negative control deletes the id-scoped rule at runtime: the bar comes back as
"1:flex", so if the fix is ever lost the control says so.

The Host's Korean was mojibake because remote60_host_app was the one target without
/utf-8. The source is UTF-8, MSVC read it in code page 949 and stored what it misread,
and C4819 had been saying so on that file for a long time. Before the flag the UTF-16
for 새 was not in the binary at all; after it, it is at 485208, and the warning count
for the target is zero. The literals were not rewritten in English and the broken text
was not frozen -- only the way the file is read changed.
